prompt: Build a full CRUD data access object over an in-memory map, with Optional lookups and id-ordered listing. Complete ProductDao.java; Product.java is provided.
explanation: A DAO gives the rest of the program ordinary Java methods -- save, findById, findAll -- and keeps the storage details in one place, so swapping this map for real JDBC would not change a single caller. Returning Optional instead of null makes "no such row" part of the method's type, and Map.remove and Map.get returning null are what let delete and update report whether anything was there. A HashMap has no order, so findAll sorts a copy of its values by id before handing it back.
hints: The map is keyed by id: save is rows.put(product.getId(), product), which also gives you replace-by-id for free.
Optional.ofNullable(rows.get(id)) turns a possibly-missing row straight into an Optional; Map.remove returns the old value, or null when there was none.
For findAll, copy rows.values() into an ArrayList and sort it with Comparator.comparingInt(Product::getId). updatePrice must read the old row first so it can keep the name.
